components.name: Agent Runtime
components.description: Managed execution environment for running AI agents on GPU-powered infrastructure. Handles orchestration, scaling, and lifecycle management for deployed agents.

components.name: Inference
components.description: Serverless access to foundation models (e.g. Llama, Mistral, GPT) via OpenAI-compatible API.

components.name: ADK
components.description: (Agent Development Kit) Open-source toolkit for building, testing, and deploying AI agents locally or in the cloud via CLI and SDK integrations.

components.name: Knowledge Bases
components.description: RAG-powered document stores that give agents access to your data. Supports multiple data sources for accurate, context-aware responses.

components.name: Guardrails
components.description: Content safety layer that filters agent inputs and outputs. Enforces topic restrictions and behavioral boundaries to keep agents on-task and compliant.

components.name: Model Services
components.description: Hosts and serves foundation and embedding models for serverless and dedicated inference workloads across the Gradient AI Platform.

incidents.name: Networking Issues in NYC1 Affecting Multiple Services
incidents.message:
Impact: minor;
## The Incident

On the evening of Wednesday, June 26th at 12:01am Eastern time, planned maintenance operations commenced on the core switches in our NYC1 datacenter to replace and add hardware which would provide additional network ports. This work was conducted as part of our ongoing efforts to maintain sufficient capacity. During this work, we determined that one of the newly installed cards had a hardware fault. In order to proceed with maintenance, some existing connections were moved to different network hardware, which meant the number of connections between the two switches - which are used to maintain high availability state and other network information - was reduced from four to two. This is still a proper supported configuration however it provides reduced redundancy. We opened a case with the vendor and expected replacement hardware within 24 hours. The planned maintenance activity completed without impact.

  

On the following morning, Wednesday June 26th, at approximately 7:20 AM eastern time we began to experience packet loss in our NYC1 datacenter. Our Engineering team began investigating the issue and identified a bug in the version of firmware running on the switches. This bug was more visible due to the reduced redundancy configuration in place. Engineers attempted to restart portions of the switch hardware that were reporting errors which resolved most of the packet loss; however, there were some residual impacts some destinations reporting problems and engineers were still noting errors in logs. To mitigate the impact we upgraded the firmware to a version that included fixes for this bug. Upgrades commenced one switch at a time, with a momentary loss of connectivity while each device of the pair came back online. Once the upgrade of the second switch was complete and fully booted, impacts from the event were fully mitigated.

The faulty hardware was replaced the next day using in-service procedures without impact.

During the primary downtime event, connectivity between Droplets, between Droplets and the Internet, and the Cloud Control Panel and API functionality was intermittently impacted, with some periods of complete unreachability.

  

## Timeline of Events

  

11:20 UTC - Our team is initially alerted to the issue  
11:30 UTC - Engineering team begins investigation

11:52 UTC - Root cause is identified and troubleshooting efforts begin

12:12-13:45 - Initial mitigation attempts begin, with incomplete results

14:10 UTC - Upgrade begins on first network device

14:48 UTC - First network device fully booted with new firmware and routing converged

14:56 UTC - Second device upgrade begins

15:22 UTC - Second network device fully booted with new firmware and routing converged

15:23 UTC - Internal alarms begin clearing, impact is over and the incident is resolved

## Future Measures

 

Our Network Engineering team is investigating additional steps and checks that can be included in our existing change plans for work done during maintenance windows. Most notably, we will be looking at defining requirements to consider a change plan successful, versus what would require a rollback of the change, and to make informed risk decisions ahead of time rather than in the midst of the activity.

## In Conclusion

We recognize the impact these networking issues had on our customers and we sincerely apologize for the frustrations and inconvenience.

incidents.name: Networking Issues in NYC3 Affecting Multiple Services
incidents.message:
Impact: major;
On June 19, DigitalOcean employees reported a network disruption impacting our NYC3 region, leading to slow-downs and timeouts on internal tools. We also received some customer reports of network disruptions, including intermittent, temporary latency or connection loss to Droplets in NYC3, as well as error messages when attempting to connect to Spaces clusters in NYC3.

DigitalOcean Support was also heavily impacted by the issue; over the duration of the incident, internal tools would not load, which lead to increased response and resolution times for tickets.

## The Incident

At approximately 12:30 PM EDT 16:30 UTC on June 19, employees reported Timeout errors when attempting to load pages in our internal systems and escalated the issue to our networking team. Shortly after that our Support and Cloud Operations teams received reports of customers being impacted when trying to use the Cloud Control Panel and API. Several engineering teams were also brought in to troubleshoot and worked throughout the day, investigating the cause of the issue. After extensive troubleshooting, we determined that the underlying issue was a change in the way one of our internal systems handled TLS X.509 certificate verification.

This change resulted in the system leaking TCP socket file handles. The remote system that the internal system was connecting to would eventually send a FIN packet to close the connection, and the TCP connection would enter a half-closed state. However, since the internal system had leaked the socket's file handle, it was not able to finish closing the connection, and the connection remained in the half-closed state indefinitely. Since the connection was not fully closed out, the NAT translation for it was retained for a longer period of time than it typically would have been, as additional communication on that connection is expected.

The internal system continued opening new connections and leaving them in this state, which eventually exhausted the available outbound ports on the NAT, resulting in services behind that NAT being unable to communicate with services in other datacenters, and also the internet at large.

## Timeline

* 18:05 UTC: Internal users report errors loading an administrative tool used for managing the DigitalOcean platform. An incident is declared to coordinate investigation and response efforts.
* 18:07 UTC: Our Support and Cloud Operations teams received reports of customers being impacted when trying to use the Cloud Control Panel and API.
* 18:35 UTC: Cloud Operations team internally escalates the incident when larger impact is observed on the DigitalOcean API, bringing in additional leadership incident management resources.
* 19:30 UTC: Network team fails over to a secondary firewall.
* 20:15 UTC: Network team isolates a core router and removes it from service to follow up on a case with the hardware vendor. Customers may have experienced intermittent, temporary packet loss to or from Droplets in NYC3 while this was happening.
* 20:55 UTC: Network team restarts one firewall in a redundant pair.
* 21:03 UTC: Network team pauses on restarting a second firewall after identifying the issue with port utilization in the NAT pool.
* 23:14 UTC: Network team identifies a billing application as contributing to higher than expected utilization on the NAT pool and their team is paged into the incident.
* 23:56 UTC: Billing team pauses the application sending this traffic, which starts to alleviate the NAT exhaustion issue.
* 00:45 UTC: Storage team migrates an internal application used for DNS services to a different region - one not encountering this NAT exhaustion issue - which helps mitigate errors for customers using the Cloud control panel and API.

## Future Measures

While we had tested the change in an internal staging environment, that environment, unfortunately, has a different network structure, and the affected traffic was not routed through a NAT, thus there was no indication of the havoc this change would cause. We are investigating a different way of using the staging environment so that we can route our traffic through a NAT, thus more completely mimicking the production environment.

For now, we have reverted the change to certificate verification and have an engineering team with investigating the best option to proceed.

## In Conclusion

We know that our service is critical in the success of your projects and businesses. We take the availability and reliability of our services very seriously, and sincerely apologize for the impact of the network disruptions.

incidents.name: SGP1 Networking Issues
incidents.message:
Impact: minor;
# The Incident

  

On May 23nd through May 26th, DigitalOcean experienced a significant increase in the amount of traffic coming into and exiting from our network. The traffic represented about a 33% increase over our normal throughput. This time period coincides almost exactly with a period of time when the country of Indonesia instituted blocks on access to a number of large social media platforms.

  

The increase in traffic was enough to temporarily exceed the total available capacity to our Singapore and Bangalore regions. We also saw significant increases in traffic in Amsterdam, and San Francisco.

  

During the time of this outage impacted customers using our Singapore and Bangalore regions may have experienced intermittent packet loss.

  

In reaction to the influx of extra traffic, our Network Engineers were able to augment our capacity to a few local providers and peers and partially mitigate the congestion issues. Additionally, DigitalOcean Network Engineering is working to establish additional connections with various transit providers to help prevent congestion in the case of this sort of event in the future.

  

In an unrelated incident, there was an upstream transit provider failure in BLR1 that caused similar symptoms of intermittent packet loss. The connections were restored by the transit provider before the influx of traffic discussed above.

# Timeline of Events

  

1:45pm May 22 UTC - The connections from DigitalOcean to one of our upstream transit providers failed causing a reroute of traffic around the failure.

  

4:30pm May 22 UTC - The upstream transit providers connections were restored.

  

12:50pm May 23 UTC - DigitalOcean Network Engineers noticed a significant increase in bandwidth used in Bangalore and Singapore regions.

  

13:00pm May 23 UTC - DigitalOcean Network Engineers adjusted network routing configurations to shift some traffic away from Telstra in SGP1 to mitigate the congestion.

  

14:00pm May 23 UTC - DigitalOcean Network Engineers added capacity to private peering with a major peering partner, shifting some traffic away from transit connections, alleviating congestion further.

  

12:30pm May 24 UTC - DigitalOcean Network Engineers added further capacity to our private peering partner to alleviate congestion further.

  

12:30pm May 26 UTC - Traffic levels returned to near normal levels.

  

# Future Measures

  

DigitalOcean engaged with transit providers to add capacity to our overall Internet transit capacity in those regions. This added capacity should be online in approximately 2-3 months, and will enable DigitalOcean to accommodate a much greater surge of traffic for an incident such as this in the future.

  

# In Conclusion

  

DigitalOcean always strives to have sufficient capacity in our network to respond seamlessly to unexpected outages and anomalous network events such as this. In this case, we did not have the available capacity in place to absorb a traffic influx of this magnitude. We will be adding capacity to avoid an incident like this in the future.

incidents.name: BLR1 Networking Issues
incidents.message:
Impact: minor;
# The Incident

  

On May 23nd through May 26th, DigitalOcean experienced a significant increase in the amount of traffic coming into and exiting from our network. The traffic represented about a 33% increase over our normal throughput. This time period coincides almost exactly with a period of time when the country of Indonesia instituted blocks on access to a number of large social media platforms.

  

The increase in traffic was enough to temporarily exceed the total available capacity to our Singapore and Bangalore regions. We also saw significant increases in traffic in Amsterdam, and San Francisco.

  

During the time of this outage impacted customers using our Singapore and Bangalore regions may have experienced intermittent packet loss.

  

In reaction to the influx of extra traffic, our Network Engineers were able to augment our capacity to a few local providers and peers and partially mitigate the congestion issues. Additionally, DigitalOcean Network Engineering is working to establish additional connections with various transit providers to help prevent congestion in the case of this sort of event in the future.

  

In an unrelated incident, there was an upstream transit provider failure in BLR1 that caused similar symptoms of intermittent packet loss. The connections were restored by the transit provider before the influx of traffic discussed above.

# Timeline of Events

  

1:45pm May 22 UTC - The connections from DigitalOcean to one of our upstream transit providers failed causing a reroute of traffic around the failure.

  

4:30pm May 22 UTC - The upstream transit providers connections were restored.

  

12:50pm May 23 UTC - DigitalOcean Network Engineers noticed a significant increase in bandwidth used in Bangalore and Singapore regions.

  

13:00pm May 23 UTC - DigitalOcean Network Engineers adjusted network routing configurations to shift some traffic away from Telstra in SGP1 to mitigate the congestion.

  

14:00pm May 23 UTC - DigitalOcean Network Engineers added capacity to private peering with a major peering partner, shifting some traffic away from transit connections, alleviating congestion further.

  

12:30pm May 24 UTC - DigitalOcean Network Engineers added further capacity to our private peering partner to alleviate congestion further.

  

12:30pm May 26 UTC - Traffic levels returned to near normal levels.

  

# Future Measures

  

DigitalOcean engaged with transit providers to add capacity to our overall Internet transit capacity in those regions. This added capacity should be online in approximately 2-3 months, and will enable DigitalOcean to accommodate a much greater surge of traffic for an incident such as this in the future.

  

# In Conclusion

  

DigitalOcean always strives to have sufficient capacity in our network to respond seamlessly to unexpected outages and anomalous network events such as this. In this case, we did not have the available capacity in place to absorb a traffic influx of this magnitude. We will be adding capacity to avoid an incident like this in the future.

incidents.name: NYC3 Spaces and CDN Performance Issues
incidents.message:
Impact: minor;
## The Incident

On May 1, 2019, the Spaces storage cluster in NYC3 suffered a cascading network interface failure. This failure caused data nodes to drop off the network and force a large segment of the cluster into data loss protection mode meaning the cluster no longer serviced writes. This resulted in a drop of S3 API availability down to ~20%.

After resetting the network hardware on the data nodes, our engineering team discovered a hardware configuration problem that blocked restoration of services above 60% of capacity until an on-premise intervention from a datacenter technician could correct the issue.

The impact of this incident was a significant disruption to data availability, with the cluster in a degraded state for approximately 2.5 hours.

## Timeline of Events

11:55 UTC - NYC3 Spaces Storage Cluster observed disruption in network traffic no loss of availability

12:01 UTC - The cluster begins recovering from initial network disruption, causing an expected spike in traffic on the backend storage network

12:06 UTC - Initial network hardware lockup detected on one data node

12:06-12:15 UTC - Additional nodes begin observing similar hardware lockup

12:16 UTC - Cluster takes data offline to prevent data loss; availability drops to 20% and the storage engineering team is paged in

12:23 UTC - Storage engineers begin diagnosing the issue and observe locked up network hardware on multiple data hosts in the cluster, resulting in full loss of connectivity between data nodes on the backend storage network

12:25-13:25 UTC - Storage engineers begin resetting network hardware to bring connectivity back up, but observe the hardware locking up again. Engineering disables the faulty hardware on all nodes down and brings only one of the network interfaces up on each data node   
  
13:30 UTC - Cluster recovers data availability back to ~60%, but exposes a hardware misconfiguration on one of the nodes

14:45 UTC - Data center team is paged to correct the hardware configuration on the misconfigured data node

14:45 UTC - Availability returns to 100% and services are fully restored

16:07 UTC - Engineering begins resetting the failed network links and bringing them back online and restore uplink redundancy

17:55 UTC - Cluster completes internal recovery back to good status

19:00 UTC - Additional alerting is put into place to catch any recurrence of the issue before it can cascade to additional nodes

## Future Measures

We have performed a full audit of all systems to ensure there are no other hardware misconfigurations. Along with the aforementioned additional alerting, we are enhancing internal processes and adding automated tooling to periodically examine the cluster configuration. Lastly, we are also working with the vendor to deploy a fix for the network hardware failure that triggered the event.

## In Conclusion

We take the stability of our services seriously and will ensure we work to improve in all areas where we can. We apologize for the inconvenience caused by this outage.
